contentBody: **In an MVP, what does viable mean?**
option.1: The page must look like a finished company before anyone is allowed to try it
option.2: Every excluded feature must still be built in full during the same sitting
option.3: A score from the model is enough to call the offer a proven product
option.4: Someone can try the core job, even if the backstage work is still manual
answerExplanation: Viable means a person can try the one job. Manual backstage work is allowed if it is honest and small. Looks and a model score are not viability.

contentBody: **When time is short, what is a safe order for changing the page?**
option.1: Put optional extras first, then the heading, then a working next step last
option.2: Clear the job, fix one next step, set expectations, then extras if they fit
option.3: A fake full product first so the page pretends later features already exist
option.4: A colour theme first, then login, then a sentence about the intended problem
answerExplanation: Change clarity first, then one honest next step, then a line on what this version is not. Extras come last, and only if they still fit the MVP.

contentBody: **A large extra feature fights a small clarity fix that fits the MVP. Time is short. What do you do?**
option.1: Do the clarity fix in this sitting and park the large extra feature for later
option.2: Build the large extra feature because a chatbot asked for it with confidence
option.3: Put both on Now, even if that blows the time box and also the include list
option.4: Do neither; spend the sitting on a new colour theme instead of the page offer
answerExplanation: When two changes fight, pick the one that protects the MVP story. Cap Now at a few items. Defer is not never; it is a parked line you can defend.
